setups.label: 120° and 125°
setups.prompt: Create two independent double-pendulum chains in parallel X-Z planes at y=-0.6 m and y=+0.6 m, each with a fixed pivot at [0,y,3.5] m. Each chain has two rigid spherical bobs of mass 1 kg and radius 0.06 m, joined by ideal massless rigid links of length 1 m. Both chains release from rest. Define signed world angle θ from the downward vertical in each X-Z plane, positive toward +X; a link vector at θ is [sin(θ),0,-cos(θ)] m. Chain A has upper angle +120° and lower angle -10°; chain B has upper angle +125° and lower angle -10°. The lower hinge of each chain must be carried by its moving upper bob as a real parent-child hinge, not an independent world hinge. Use zero hinge stiffness and damping, zero friction and drag, Earth gravity [0,0,-9.81] m/s², and a real ground at z=0 m with restitution 1 and zero friction; bob restitution is 0. Use distinct chain colors, plain studio appearance and no reference grid.
setups.summary: Two parallel double pendulums start at rest, with upper links at 120° and 125° and both lower links at −10°.
assumptions: Ideal massless links are represented by hinges; each lower hinge is attached to its moving upper bob.
Angles are absolute world angles measured from downward vertical toward +X; all bobs start at rest.
setups.note: Run for four seconds, then compare the blue and red lower bobs.

title: A spring net catches a ball
question: Can a net catch and relaunch a falling ball?

setups.label: A 1.5 kg ball over an elastic net
setups.prompt: Create a square spring-net impact experiment under Earth gravity [0,0,-9.81] m/s², with a real non-rebounding frictionless ground at z=0. A fixed rectangular frame is centered at [0,0,1.8] m: four 0.08 m square-section beams at x=±0.94 or y=±0.94, full length 1.96 m, with four 0.08×0.08×1.76 m fixed legs at [±0.94,±0.94,0.88]. Make a 5×5 grid of spherical junctions radius 0.045 m at [(c−2)0.45,(r−2)0.45,1.8] m for integer r,c=0..4. Fix the perimeter junctions (r or c is 0 or 4); the nine interior junctions are free rigid bodies of mass 0.08 kg each. All start at rest. Connect nearest horizontal/vertical neighboring junction centers with linear spring tendons of stiffness 70 N/m; connect both diagonals of every square with 40 N/m springs. Omit links whose two endpoints are both fixed. Every spring has rest length 0.88 times its initial straight-line distance and damping 0.2 N·s/m. This is an explicitly pretensioned discrete network, not cloth or a stress/strain simulation. Show thin coils with wire radius 0.004 m, coil radius 0.018 m and five turns. Put a rigid 1.5 kg ball of radius 0.30 m at [0,0,3.25] m, initially held by the fixed north frame beam. Schedule one native release at 1.2 s with no launch impulse. All contact restitution and all friction coefficients are zero; add no air drag or other loads. Only the network springs store elastic energy; the ball itself does not deform. Use an orange ball, blue moving junctions, muted frame and daylight over a concrete ground.
setups.summary: A scheduled drop loads a pretensioned spring network, which deflects and returns stored elastic energy.
assumptions: The net is nine moving rigid junctions and 52 linear spring links tied to a fixed perimeter, not a continuous membrane.
Spring rest lengths are 12% shorter than the initial spans; contact is inelastic and frictionless.
The initially held ball becomes visible when released at 1.2 s; frame and ground are fixed.

scene.title: A spring net catches a ball

setups.note: Drops at 1.2 s. The ball is inelastic; the springs return stored energy.

title: Three-body figure eight
question: Can three equal point masses repeat a figure eight under mutual gravity alone?

setups.label: Three equal point masses
setups.prompt: Create a groundless space model with a readable XY plane and z=0. Use three world-root ideal point particles with equal mass m=14,982,844,642.8839 kg (1/G), and one mutual-gravity load acting on exactly those three particles with G=6.67430e-11 N·m²/kg². Set uniform gravity to [0,0,0] m/s². Start the blue particle at [-0.97000436,0.24308753,0] m with velocity [0.466203685,0.432365730,0] m/s; the orange particle at [0.97000436,-0.24308753,0] m with velocity [0.466203685,0.432365730,0] m/s; and the teal particle at [0,0,0] m with velocity [-0.93240737,-0.86473146,0] m/s. Add no drag, ground, other loads, central body, or prescribed path. Show each particle's trajectory trail from the existing renderer. This is an ideal point-mass lab-display scale: Gm=1 m³/s² gives a metre-scale orbit with a period of about 6.326 s. The particles have no physical radius; these values are not finite stars or a precision astronomy model.
setups.summary: Three equal ideal point masses chase one another around a planar figure eight under mutual gravity alone.
assumptions: Each moving body is an ideal point particle with no physical radius or collision surface.
The large equal masses and metre-scale orbit are a lab-display scale, not a model of finite stars.
The XY plane has no uniform gravity or drag; native mutual gravity is the only load.
setups.note: Run for about 6.3 seconds. Switch to Speed to compare the changing velocities.

title: The frictionless loop
question: Can a frictionless track still slow a bead?

setups.label: Same speed, different impacts
setups.prompt: Build a vertical 32-panel polygonal loop with two separate free spherical beads under Earth gravity [0,0,-9.81] m/s². The loop center is [0,0,1.35] m. For i=0..31 use φ=-90°+11.25°i, panel center [1.03 cosφ,0,1.35+1.03 sinφ] m, full box size [0.197967721,0.54,0.06] m, and quaternion [cos(α/2),0,sin(α/2),0] in w,x,y,z order with α=-φ-90°. All 32 panels are fixed, with normal restitution 1. Their real corners are intentional: this is a polygonal impact track, not a smooth rail. Each bead has mass 0.15 kg, radius 0.055 m and no initial spin. The blue elastic bead starts at [0,-0.17,0.405] m with restitution 1; the orange inelastic bead starts at [0,+0.17,0.405] m with restitution 0. Give both initial world velocity [10,0,0] m/s. Set all sliding, static, torsional and rolling friction coefficients to zero for beads, panels and ground. Include a fixed ground at z=0 with restitution 0. Add no air drag, additional viscous damping, hinges, guides, forces, scheduled impulses or prescribed paths. The separated lanes are established by their initial geometry, not a constraint. Compare energy transfer at panel impacts: zero friction does not eliminate normal-impact losses. Both beads are free rigid bodies and can leave the panel surfaces. Use blue and orange beads, muted panels, a plain visual ground, daylight and no reference grid; appearance must not change the declared contact coefficients.
setups.summary: Equal-speed beads meet the same frictionless polygonal track, but only the orange bead absorbs energy in normal impacts.
assumptions: The track has 32 real flat panels and corners, not an ideal smooth circular guide.
All friction is zero. Panel and blue-bead restitution targets are 1; orange-bead and ground restitution targets are 0.
Both beads start at 10 m/s with no spin or air drag. No joint keeps either bead on the track.
setups.note: Both start at 10 m/s. Compare their paths after three seconds.

title: Dominoes around a bend
question: How does a fall travel around a curve?

setups.label: Twenty dominoes around a bend
setups.prompt: Create a chain of 20 independent free rigid wooden domino blocks on a fixed level ground plane at z=0 m. Use Earth gravity [0,0,-9.81] m/s². Each block is a uniform rectangular solid with full dimensions 0.036 m along its local X (the path direction), 0.012 m along local Y, and 0.180 m high along local Z, mass 0.055 kg, and initially zero linear and angular velocity. Place their upright center stations on a circular arc in the XY plane: radius 0.85943669 m, equal 5° tangent turns and 0.075 m arc spacing. For block number i=0,…,19, set φ=i×5°; center x=R sinφ, y=R(1−cosφ), yaw=φ, and upright center z=0.090 m. Give only the first block a 14° initial tip toward the second along local +X; rotate about local Y after its yaw, and raise its center only enough to put its lowest bottom corner at z=0: z=0.090 cos14°+0.018 sin14°=0.09168121 m. Keep all other blocks exactly upright. Adjacent centers are 0.075 m apart along the arc, leaving a clear initial gap; do not add pivots, joints, scheduled actions, impulses, loads, additional viscous damping, air drag, or other moving bodies. Use zero restitution for the blocks and ground, sliding friction 0.55 and static friction 0.70 for both, and zero torsional and rolling friction. All motion after release must arise only from gravity and native block-to-block and block-to-ground contact. Use a concrete visual ground, daylight and no reference grid; these cosmetic choices must not change the stated friction.
setups.summary: A single gravity-driven tip travels through 20 free blocks on a circular arc.
assumptions: Each domino is a uniform rigid wooden block with the stated dimensions and mass.
Contact friction and zero restitution are native solver targets; no other forces, damping or scheduled motions act.
setups.note: Only the first block starts tilted. The fall reaches the far end in about 2.5 s.
